families.name: Normative Climate & Informal Enforcement
families.definition: Group-level behavioral regularities, expressed approval patterns, and informal reinforcement conditions that make conduct more or less socially expected.
families.includes: Observed behavioral prevalence, publicly expressed approval, consensus, trends, visibility, and informal social rewards or sanctions.
families.exclusions: An individual's perceived norms (Psychological), deeply shared cultural meanings (Cultural), and formal rules or penalties (Institutional / Structural).

families.name: Direct Social Influence Conditions
families.definition: Observable properties of other people and influence settings that change the social evidence, pressure, or models available to an actor.
families.includes: Majority size and unanimity, minority consistency, peer presence and exposure, and socially relevant model similarity or status.
families.exclusions: Conformity itself, internal normative or informational influence mechanisms, persuasion judgments, and message-content properties.

families.name: Interaction & Relational Embeddedness
families.definition: Properties of recurring interpersonal interaction and dyadic ties that determine access, obligation, familiarity, and relational constraint.
families.includes: Interaction amount, relationship duration and stability, closeness, reciprocity, multiplexity, and negative interaction frequency.
families.exclusions: Perceived belonging or trust, network-wide topology, formal role assignments, and one-off behavior without a relational state.

families.name: Inclusion, Support & Social Integration
families.definition: Observable access to relationships, supportive transactions, participation, and exclusion that embed or isolate an actor within a social system.
families.includes: Personal-network size and breadth, support availability and receipt, inclusion and ostracism events, and objective social isolation.
families.exclusions: Perceived support, loneliness, belonging, attachment needs, and clinical or health outcomes.

families.name: Cooperation, Reciprocity & Mutual Dependence
families.definition: Relational conditions governing reliable exchange, mutual aid, repeated cooperation, resource sharing, and vulnerability to free riding.
families.includes: Partner reliability, cooperation prevalence, reciprocity balance, repeated interaction, mutual aid, resource sharing, and free-riding prevalence.
families.exclusions: Interpersonal trust or fairness appraisals, prosocial traits, formal contracts, and cooperation as an unanalyzed behavioral outcome.

families.name: Status, Reputation & Relational Power
families.definition: Socially conferred rank, standing, deference, and asymmetric control that structure whose preferences and actions carry weight.
families.includes: Status rank and hierarchy shape, reputation, deference, resource or dependence asymmetry, and informal authority.
families.exclusions: Status motives or perceived status (Psychological), demographic labels, and authority defined solely by law or office (Institutional / Structural).

families.name: Network Structure & Position
families.definition: Graph-level and actor-position variables describing connectivity, closure, brokerage, assortative mixing, and separation in social networks.
families.includes: Recognized network measures with explicit relational meaning, including centrality, density, clustering, constraint, cross-cluster ties, and segregation.
families.exclusions: Platform algorithms, raw trace counts without a defined network, perceived network position, and diffusion outcomes.

families.name: Network Exposure & Social Diffusion
families.definition: Relational exposure conditions through which behaviors, practices, and social signals reach an actor through a network.
families.includes: Proportion, frequency, independence, reinforcement, referent influence, and cross-cluster composition of network exposure.
families.exclusions: Information accuracy or framing, algorithmic ranking, adoption behavior itself, and influence inferred from observational similarity alone.

families.name: Group Composition, Cohesion & Deliberation
families.definition: Properties of bounded groups that shape participation, information pooling, dissent, subgroup formation, and sustained joint activity.
families.includes: Group size, cohesion, turnover, roles, opinion diversity, dissent availability, participation equality, shared-information coverage, and factionalization.
families.exclusions: Individual identity or emotion, performance outcomes, formal governance rules, and group labels without a varying property.

families.name: Coordination, Accountability & Collective Capacity
families.definition: Group-level conditions that make coordinated action feasible by aligning goals, expectations, knowledge, roles, responsibility, and answerability.
families.includes: Task interdependence, goal alignment, common knowledge, expectation alignment, collective efficacy, role clarity, identifiable contributions, responsibility concentration, and peer accountability.
families.exclusions: Individual self-efficacy or intentions, formal compliance systems, communication-channel properties, and collective action outcomes.

families.name: Audience & Social Evaluation
families.definition: Observable social-evaluation conditions created when other people can witness, identify, monitor, or evaluate an actor and an action.
families.includes: Audience presence and size, actor identifiability, action publicness, evaluation exposure, and peer monitoring intensity.
families.exclusions: Evaluation apprehension or reputational concern (Psychological), sensor surveillance (Technological), and formal audit regimes (Institutional / Structural).

families.name: Intergroup Contact, Boundaries & Competition
families.definition: Relational conditions connecting or separating social groups and governing contact, friendship, cooperation, competition, interdependence, and relative position between them.
families.includes: Intergroup contact and friendship, cross-group ties, competition and cooperation, resource interdependence, boundary permeability, inequality, and cross-cutting memberships.
families.exclusions: Threat, prejudice, anxiety, identification, or outgroup evaluation (Psychological), cultural meanings, and formal segregation policies.

frozenRecord.name: Behavioral Prevalence

frozenRecord.mechanism: Provides externally observable social evidence about what is common, feasible, or locally adaptive and can update perceived descriptive norms.
frozenRecord.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Reference-group relevance, visibility, credibility, identity, observability, culture, and conflict between descriptive and injunctive signals.
frozenRecord.persistenceRecovery: May shift quickly after salient public change but can persist through repeated reinforcement.
frozenRecord.measurementAssessmentMethods: Behavioral observation; representative group survey; content coding; field experiment; longitudinal prevalence tracking
frozenRecord.measurementCaveats: A measured group condition depends on the specified reference group, behavior, setting, and time window; individual perception may differ substantially.
